newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel plans Arab East Jerusalem projects.
newsitem.headline: Israel plans Arab East Jerusalem projects.

text.p: Israel will improve services and infrastructure for Arabs in East Jerusalem, where Palestinians hope to establish the capital of a future state, a cabinet minister said on Sunday.

Police Minister Avigdor Kahalani was commenting on a report in the Haaretz newspaper that Israel planned to improve conditions for Arabs of East Jerusalem to strengthen its self-declared sovereignty over all of the city.
"We found...we have a real difference between the west Jerusalem (and) the east," Kahalani told Israel Radio, referring to government facilities available to the holy city's Arabs and Jews.

"We are going to support the (Israeli) municipality and the mayor to build many things in the east," he said. "We are not going to control the religious places and we are not going to convince the Moslem to be a Zionist...but we are going to give the same opportunities...to the people who live in the east."
Kahalani did not mention any specific projects.

Haaretz said an interministerial committee he heads proposed opening another Israeli police station and branches of government offices in East Jerusalem as well as building a new sewer system, repaving roads and constructing more classrooms.
"Any unilateral steps from the side of Israel will add another obstacle to peace," Palestinian official Ziyad Abu Ziyad said in response to Kahalani's plans.

"There is no chance for any stability or any real peace in the Middle East if the Israelis will continue to ignore the rights and the feelings of the Moslems and Christians in the city of Jerusalem," Ziyad told the radio.

The opening by Israel's right-wing government of a new entrance to an archaeological tunnel near Moslem holy sites in East Jerusalem in September touched off five days of Palestinian rage in which 60 Arabs and 15 Israelis were killed.

Israel, which captured the Arab eastern part of the city in 1967 along with the rest of the West Bank, claims all Jerusalem as its capital. The PLO wants East Jerusalem to be the capital of a future Palestinian state.

Under a 1993 deal, Israel and the PLO agreed to discuss the city's future only after the current interim stage of peace is completed and not to take any measures to change the character of the city before a permanent settlement is reached.

Asked if Israel was creating "facts on the ground" to preempt a final agreement with the Palestinians, Kahalani told the radio: "We have decided that Jerusalem will be united forever and this is the capital of Israel.
"I hope they will never have a Palestinian state but if they create a Palestinian state, the capital will be maybe Ramallah, not Jerusalem."
